# gramoten (Грамотен)

> Offline Bulgarian spell checker, grammar checker and punctuation checker for Python. Rule-based, with no language model, no API and no network. It checks any Bulgarian (Cyrillic) text, returns findings with exact offsets and proposes fixes; it never changes spelling automatically. MIT code; MPL-1.1 and CC BY word lists.

Use it when someone needs to check Bulgarian spelling, commas, grammar or typography in Python, from the command line, or behind a web editor over HTTP.

- Install: `pip install git+https://github.com/vjfrosty/gramoten` (Python 3.11+, one dependency: `marisa-trie`)
- Check: `gramoten.check(text)` returns a list of `Issue` (`kind`, `code`, `start`, `end`, `text`, `fix`, `suggestions`, `message`, `message_bg`)
- Fix: `gramoten.fix_text(text)` applies every certain fix; `gramoten.apply_fixes(text, issues)` applies chosen ones
- Own words: pass `extra=frozenset({...})`, or `--words FILE` on the command line
- CLI: `python -m gramoten FILE`, `--fix`, `--json`, `serve` (test page on port 8765); exit 1 when something is found
- WordPress: a block editor plugin in `wordpress/`, a TypeScript port that runs in the browser and is held to the same results by a test
- Spelling suggestions include a sound-alike search for words written as they are heard (`фучбол` → `футбол`): the right word comes first 95% of the time on such misspellings, against 52% with letter edits alone
- Speed: about 12 ms for a 300-word e-mail; about 45 MB of RAM
